note: Trivial submodule of purge_purger_http. Provides one Purge TagsHeader plugin PurgeCacheTagsHeader (@PurgeTagsHeader id=purge_tagsheader, header_name=Purge-Cache-Tags), extending TagsHeaderBase with an empty body. Purge core's tagsheaders registry attaches the header to cacheable responses. Depends only on purge. No config, form, route, permission, schema or Drush - enabling the module is the entire setup. Introspection reads the live tagsheader plugin definition (header name / plugin id) via plugin.manager.purge.tagsheader; execution enables the module so the Purge-Cache-Tags header plugin is registered, verified against live module + plugin state.

evals.prompt: What response header does the purge_purger_http_tagsheader submodule make Drupal emit, and what is it for?
evals.expected_output: It emits the Purge-Cache-Tags response header listing each response's Drupal cache tags, so a tag-aware reverse proxy or CDN can invalidate cached objects by cache tag.

evals.prompt: Which Purge plugin type and plugin id does purge_purger_http_tagsheader provide, and does it have any configuration?
evals.expected_output: It provides a Purge TagsHeader plugin (@PurgeTagsHeader) with id purge_tagsheader (class PurgeCacheTagsHeader extends TagsHeaderBase). It has no configuration - enabling the module is the whole setup.

evals.prompt: When do you need the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module, and how does it fit with the Generic HTTP Purger?
evals.expected_output: You only need it for custom setups under your own control, where a reverse proxy/CDN reads the Purge-Cache-Tags header to remember which tags a cached object depends on; the parent Generic HTTP Purger then sends the requests (e.g. a BAN) that invalidate those tags.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site, inspect the Purge tags-header plugins and state the name of the response header that the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module registers.
evals.expected_output: The purge_tagsheader plugin (from plugin.manager.purge.tagsheader) declares header_name = Purge-Cache-Tags.

evals.prompt: Inspect the registered Purge TagsHeader plugins on this live site and give the plugin id contributed by the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module.
evals.expected_output: The plugin id is purge_tagsheader (class PurgeCacheTagsHeader), discoverable via the plugin.manager.purge.tagsheader plugin manager.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site should expose its cache tags to a downstream proxy via the Purge-Cache-Tags response header, using the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module. Make it so on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Enable the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module (e.g. drush en purge_purger_http_tagsheader -y). Once enabled, its purge_tagsheader TagsHeader plugin (header_name Purge-Cache-Tags) is registered and Purge attaches the header to cacheable responses.

evals.prompt: I want my Drupal pages to tell my caching proxy which cache tags each page uses (via the Purge-Cache-Tags header) so it can clear the right pages. Turn on whatever part of the Generic HTTP Purger provides that header.
evals.expected_output: Same verified end state as purge_purger_http_tagsheader-enable: the purge_purger_http_tagsheader module is enabled and the purge_tagsheader plugin (Purge-Cache-Tags) is registered.
